nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on a finite vertex set, let $u(H)$ be the number of spanning subgraphs of $H$ that are isomorphic to no other spanning subgraph of $H$ (its unique subgraphs). There is no real constant $c > 0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ some graph $H$ on $n$ vertices has $u(H) \ge c \cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}} / n!$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 426 is false (Bradač–Christoph)

nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on a finite vertex set, let $u(H)$ be the number of spanning subgraphs of $H$ that are isomorphic to no other spanning subgraph of $H$ (its unique subgraphs). The statement is that there is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ some graph $H$ on $n$ vertices has $u(H) \ge c \cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}} / n!$.
nodes.title: Many unique subgraphs (Erdős Problem 426)

nodes.summary: For a graph $H$ on a finite vertex set, let $u(H)$ be the number of spanning subgraphs of $H$ that are isomorphic to no other spanning subgraph of $H$. This is the proposition that there is no real constant $c > 0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ some graph $H$ on $n$ vertices has $u(H) \ge c \cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}} / n!$.
nodes.title: Negation of the Erdős Problem 426 statement

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on the same vertex set $V$. Then $G$ is a unique subgraph of $H$ if exactly one subgraph of $H$ is isomorphic to $G$. Here a subgraph of $H$ means a spanning subgraph: a graph on $V$ all of whose edges are edges of $H$ (not necessarily induced).
nodes.title: Unique subgraph

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a graph on a finite vertex set $V$. The number of unique subgraphs of $H$ is the number of spanning subgraphs $G$ of $H$ (graphs on $V$ all of whose edges are edges of $H$) that are unique subgraphs of $H$, that is, isomorphic to no other spanning subgraph of $H$.
nodes.title: Number of unique subgraphs
